methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective two-center biomarker/cohort study (n=119 de novo FL, 25 paired relapse samples, 16 tFL) using targeted NGS to estimate TMB. The design is appropriate for exploring prognostic associations, and standard analyses (Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn/Bonferroni, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Cox regression with PH assumption checked) are correctly applied with C-index/CPE/BIC/AIC used for model comparison. Important weaknesses: no a priori power calculation is reported; the TMB cutoff (2.55 mut/Mb) is derived data-dependently via maxstat on the same cohort used for survival analysis without an independent validation set, which inflates optimism; the low-TMB subgroup is small (14.3%, ~17 patients) producing wide CIs; no formal multiplicity correction for the many clinical/genetic associations tested; and the authors note that individual variants contribute ~0.8 mut/Mb, so a 2.55 cutoff is sensitive to a handful of calls. FFPE deamination score reporting is a strength, but variant filtering and artefact handling are only partially described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study of a prognostic biomarker, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. It targets a clinically important unmet need - identifying POD24 patients at diagnosis - and reports patient-relevant endpoints (PFS, LSS, OS). The translational implication (adding TMB on top of FLIPI, potentially informing ICI priming strategies) is plausible but not demonstrated: there is no external validation cohort, no decision-curve or net-reclassification analysis, and the data-driven cutoff of 2.55 mut/Mb is not independently validated. Clinical actionability is further limited by the paradoxical direction (low TMB = worse outcome, limiting the ICI-neoantigen framing used in the discussion) and by the modest effect size relative to FLIPI.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the applicable standard as this is a prognostic biomarker study. Many REMARK items are addressed - clinical cohort description (Table 1), treatment, endpoint definitions, assay details (gene panel, read depth, variant filters, deamination score), multivariable modelling with FLIPI, and acknowledged limitations. However, important items are missing or weak: no patient flow diagram, no explicit pre-specification of hypotheses/cutoff, incomplete reporting of missing data and attrition (23/116 vs 119 denominators for POD24 are not fully explained), no reproducibility/validation cohort, and no formal REMARK checklist. Data and code availability are not stated in the blinded text; sequencing data deposition in a public repository (e.g., EGA/dbGaP) is not mentioned, and no analytical code is referenced, hence a low reproducibility score.

novelty_literature.justification: The question - TMB as a prognostic biomarker in FL - fills a documented gap, as the authors correctly identify only one directly comparable prior FL study (Tsukamoto et al. using WES). The contribution is a meaningful empirical extension: panel-based TMB in a reasonably sized FL cohort, correlation with t(14;18), BCL2, TNFRSF14 and GNA13/GNAI2, and paired diagnosis-relapse dynamics in 25 patients. However, novelty is incremental: TMB as prognostic in solid tumours and in DLBCL is well established and heavily cited (refs 16, 17, 36-38); the panel-based approach itself is not new; and the finding that low (rather than high) TMB predicts worse outcome, while interesting, is not mechanistically resolved. No new assay, model system, or conceptual framework is introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear IMRaD structure, a lay-plus-structured abstract, and a logical results flow from mutational landscape to TMB prognostic value to relapse dynamics and tFL. Terminology is defined (POD24, FLIPI variants, m7-FLIPI), acronyms are expanded on first use, and the discussion appropriately contextualizes findings against Tsukamoto et al. and DLBCL TMB literature. Minor issues: some sentences are long and the discussion occasionally restates results (e.g., GNA13/GNAI2 associations), the denominator for POD24 (23/116 vs 119) is not explained, and figure/table captions as described are not always self-contained (e.g., Figure 4A,B stratification variables are listed in text, not clearly in caption).

key_strengths: Addresses a documented unmet need (POD24 identification) in a reasonably sized de novo FL cohort (n=119) with long follow-up and standard first-line immunochemotherapy
Multivariable Cox models with proper PH checking and multiple performance metrics (C-index, CPE, BIC, AIC) demonstrate TMB adds information beyond FLIPI
Includes paired diagnosis-relapse analysis in 25 patients, adding clonal-evolution insights uncommon in biomarker studies
Mutational landscape (CREBBP, KMT2D, BCL2, EZH2) is consistent with established FL genetics, supporting assay validity
Clear, well-structured writing with appropriate contextualization against the single prior FL TMB study (Tsukamoto et al.) and DLBCL literature
key_concerns: Data-driven TMB cutoff (2.55 mut/Mb) derived by maxstat on the same cohort used for survival analysis, with no independent validation cohort - substantial optimism bias
Low-TMB subgroup is only ~17 patients (14.3%), producing wide CIs and limiting the robustness of multivariable adjustment

No power calculation, no explicit multiplicity correction across the many clinical/genetic associations tested, and incomplete handling of missing data (POD24 denominator 23/116 vs cohort 119 unexplained)
No statement of data or code availability; sequencing data deposition and analysis scripts are not referenced, limiting reproducibility

Mechanistic interpretation is strained: low TMB predicting worse outcome runs counter to the neoantigen/ICI framing emphasized in the discussion, and tFL cohort (n=16) is underpowered for any survival inference
REMARK checklist not formally addressed; no patient-flow diagram and no pre-specification of cutoff/hypotheses
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent, clinically relevant retrospective biomarker study with a meaningful incremental finding, but limited by a data-driven cutoff without external validation, a small low-TMB subgroup, and absent data/code sharing - placing it in Tier 3 (BMC Cancer / BJC / IJC class) with minor revisions rather than Tier 2.
